title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 16
statement: In Coinland, there are three types of coins, each worth \(6,\) \(10,\) and \(15.\) What is the sum of the digits of the maximum amount of money that is impossible to have?

solutions.text:
The amounts \(30,31,32,33,34,35\) are all attainable (for instance \(30=6\cdot 5,\) \(31=6+10+15,\) \(32=6\cdot 2+10\cdot 2,\) \(33=6\cdot 3+15,\) \(34=6\cdot 4+10,\) \(35=10+10+15\)). Adding \(6\)’s then reaches every larger amount. Checking below, \(29\) is impossible: without a \(15\)-coin a sum of \(6\)’s and \(10\)’s is even, while with one \(15\)-coin the remaining \(14\) cannot be written as \(6a+10b;\) two \(15\)-coins already exceed \(29.\) So the largest impossible amount is \(29,\) whose digit sum is \(2+9=11.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
